# 1 Maccabees Chapter 15 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 15 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_015_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Antiochus son of Demetrius the king sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon the priest and ethnarch of the Jews and to all the nation,

**2** and their contents were as follows: "King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and ethnarch and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

**3** Whereas certain pestilent men have seized the kingdom of our fathers, I intend to reclaim it so that I may restore it as it was before; and I have recruited a great army and have provided warships,

**4** and I intend to go through the country so that I may take vengeance on those who have destroyed our country and have laid waste many cities in our kingdom.

**5** Now therefore I confirm to you all the tax-remissions that the kings before me granted you, and whatever other gifts they gave you,

**6** and I give you permission to coin money for your country with your own stamp.

**7** Jerusalem and the sanctuary shall be free; and all the arms that you have prepared and all the strongholds that you have built and that you hold — let them be yours.

**8** And whatever is owed to the royal treasury and whatever is to be due to it hereafter — from this time and forever, let these be released for you.

**9** And when we have established our kingdom, we will honor you and your nation and the temple with great honor, so that your glory will be known throughout the earth."

**10** In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year Antiochus went into the land of his fathers, and all the forces joined him, so that few were left with Trypho.

**11** And Antiochus pursued him, and he came fleeing to Dor which is by the sea.

**12** For he knew that troubles had come upon him and his forces had left him.

**13** And Antiochus encamped against Dor with a hundred and twenty thousand men of war and eight thousand cavalry;

**14** and he surrounded the city, and the ships joined the battle from the sea, and he pressed the city hard from land and sea and let no one enter or leave.

**15** And Numenius came from Rome, he and his companions, having letters to the kings and to the countries in these contents:

**16** "Lucius consul of the Romans to King Ptolemy, greetings.

**17** The envoys of the Jews came to us as friends and allies, to renew the ancient friendship and alliance, sent by Simon the high priest and the Jewish people.

**18** And they brought a golden shield of a thousand minas.

**19** We resolved therefore to write to the kings and the countries that they should not plot against them or fight against them or their cities and their country, and that they should not assist those who fight against them.

**20** And we resolved to accept the shield from them.

**21** If therefore any pestilent men have fled from their country to you, hand them over to Simon the high priest so that he may punish them according to their law."

**22** He wrote the same things also to Demetrius the king and Attalus and Ariarathes and Arsaces,

**23** and to all the countries — Sampsames and the Spartans and Delos and Myndos and Sicyon and Caria and Samos and Pamphylia and Lycia and Halicarnassus and Cos and Side and Aradus and Rhodes and Phaselis and Gortyna and Cnidus and Cyprus and Cyrene.

**24** And a copy of these letters they wrote to Simon the high priest.

**25** And Antiochus the king besieged Dor the second time, continually bringing his forces against it and making engines of war, and he shut up Trypho from going out or coming in.

**26** And Simon sent to him two thousand chosen men to fight for him, and silver and gold and much equipment.

**27** But he refused to accept them, and he annulled all the agreements that had been made with him previously, and he was estranged from him.

**28** And he sent to him Athenobius one of his friends to negotiate with him, saying: "You are holding Joppa and Gazara and the citadel in Jerusalem, which are cities of my kingdom.

**29** Their borders you have devastated and you have done great harm to the land, and you have gotten control of many places in my kingdom.

**30** Now therefore hand over the cities which you have seized and the tribute of the places which you have occupied outside the borders of Judea,

**31** or else give five hundred talents of silver for the destruction which you have caused and five hundred talents more for the tribute of the cities; otherwise we will come and make war against you."

**32** And Athenobius the king's friend came to Jerusalem and saw the glory of Simon and the cupboard with gold and silver vessels and his great retinue, and he was amazed; and he reported to him the king's words.

**33** And Simon answered and said to him: "We have not taken foreign land nor have we seized foreign property, but only the inheritance of our fathers, which for a time was unjustly held by our enemies.

**34** But we, as the opportunity presented itself, have held fast to the inheritance of our fathers.

**35** But as for Joppa and Gazara which you demand, they were doing great harm among the people and to our land; we will give you a hundred talents for them."

**36** And Athenobius answered him not a word, but returned in anger to the king, and reported to him these words and the glory of Simon and all that he had seen; and the king was greatly angry.

**37** And Trypho embarked on a ship and fled to Orthosia.

**38** And the king appointed Cendebaeus governor of the seacoast and gave him troops of infantry and cavalry.

**39** And he commanded him to encamp against Judea and to build Kidron and to fortify the gates and to make war against the people; and the king pursued Trypho.

**40** And Cendebaeus came to Jamnia and began to provoke the people and to invade Judea and to take people captive and to kill them.

**41** And he built Kidron and stationed there cavalry and troops, so that they might go out and make forays along the roads of Judea, as the king had ordered him.
